extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: MathVista is a benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering seven mathematical reasoning types and five primary tasks across diverse visual contexts.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MathVista was collected by aggregating 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA and 19 VQA datasets) and creating 3 new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select math-related examples, followed by expert human annotation. New datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to heterogeneity of source datasets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets), plus 3 newly created datasets. IQTest sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms; FunctionQA from functional plots; PaperQA from academic papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA sourced from papers released in August 2023; Bard evaluation: Sep 8–10, 2023; GPT-4V evaluation: Oct 7–15, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning (numeric answers or quantity words). This yielded 4,949 examples, then expert annotators manually labeled them using majority voting. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples. The dataset was split into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) using a stratified sampling strategy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For VQA datasets, three expert annotators manually labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. For the three new datasets, graduate students in STEM fields annotated questions, with a two-step process: independent annotation by three reviewers followed by discussion to resolve disagreements. For mathematical reasoning category labels, expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples from seven candidates to verify automatic annotation quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement for VQA mathematical reasoning labeling was measured using Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 (substantial agreement). For the three new datasets, inter-annotation consistency rate was 99.2%, with only 6 out of 736 questions showing disagreements. For automatic mathematical reasoning category annotation, 94.1% of examples matched human annotations exactly, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 annotators per item (for VQA labeling and new dataset annotation); 5 annotators per item (for human performance baseline)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: New dataset annotators: graduate students in STEM fields. Human performance annotators (AMT): required high school diploma or higher, history of more than 5,000 HIT tasks completed, acceptance score higher than 0.99.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: EasyOCR (for OCR text detection); GPT-4 (for answer extraction)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination; an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process with commitment to refining data noise and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Scalability and generalizability to other domains is a concern. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations, and annotations lack unified format. The benchmark focuses on the most recent and prominent models only. Advanced topics such as college curricula limit human performance to 60.3%.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation/benchmarking of LLMs and LMMs on mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. The testmini subset (1,000 examples) is intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources. The test set (5,141 examples) is for standard evaluation.

name.evidence: we present MATHVISTA, a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks.

description.evidence: It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA).

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: One limitation is the dataset coverage. While MATHVISTA encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals... the scalability and generalizability of our benchmark to other domains remain a concern. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples (Table 1) having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure... Given the rapid development in foundation models, our study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: testmini contains 1,000 examples, intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources. The test set features the remaining 5,141 examples for standard evaluation... to (1) facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios, and (2) evaluate the research progress of LLMs and LMMs, especially their capabilities in solving rigorous reasoning tasks.
